mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has stabilized at elevated levels (38.6–54.9% above baseline) over the past four weeks, indicating sustained outdoor recreation preference. This substitution effect crowds out indoor retail-and-recreation visits, suppressing RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mean over t-3w to t-0w is 47.8, consistently above 38%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points over the next 28 days despite PARKS remaining above 35% baseline.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has recovered from -28.4% to -25.7% over the past four weeks, signaling gradual return of commuting confidence. This week-on-week improvement in TRANSIT will drive RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks as commuters resume incidental shopping.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 1.5 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -26% in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines despite TRANSIT improvement.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains flat and low (2.6–3.4% above baseline), indicating suppressed essential shopping. When combined with stable RESIDENTIAL elevation (0.9–2.1%), this signals households are minimizing all out-of-home trips. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as the cautious-mobility regime persists.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM variance is 0.8 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -8% over the next 28 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain below 4% and 2.5% respectively.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained stable at approximately -19.5% over four weeks with negligible variance (0.6 points). This persistent suppression indicates ongoing workplace restrictions or remote-work adoption. Absent workplace recovery, RETAIL_REC will not recover, as workplace-adjacent retail depends on commuter density.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains between -20% and -19% for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES range is -19.9 to -19.3 over t-1w and t-0w
regime_hint: tightening restrictions or persistent remote work
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES remains below -18%.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has oscillated narrowly between -13.9% and -11.9% over four weeks, exhibiting mean reversion tendency. The most recent value (-11.9%, t-0w) is the highest in the series. This upward tick, if sustained, signals emerging consumer confidence that will drive RETAIL_REC toward baseline over the next week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises above -12% in the current week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC at t-0w is -11.9%, highest in four-week window
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls below -13% in the next week, or remains flat at -11.9% or lower for two consecutive weeks.

fact:TRANSIT mean is -27.1 over four weeks

This outbound shift, combined with stable GROCERY_PHARM (2.6%), suggests consumers are reallocating time to non-essential activities. This bifurcation will limit RETAIL_REC recovery to transit-dependent retail only, producing net suppression over four weeks.
